newsitem.title: ITALY: Italian families less pessimistic on economy-Isco.
newsitem.headline: Italian families less pessimistic on economy-Isco.

text.p: Families are less pessimistic this month than in April about their economic prospects but are still worried about unemployment, a study by Italy's research institute for economic conditions (Isco) said on Monday.
An index that measures families' confidence in the economy rose to 109.4 from 108.1 in April, although it fell from last May's 114.8, according to the study.

"There is a net containment of pessimism" over the prospects of the Italian economy in the next 12 months and less apprehension about prices, Isco said. But there is still considerable worry about unemployment, it said.
The jobless rate in Italy stood at 12.4 percent of the workforce in January, according to official figures.
Consumers remain cautious about short-term spending, although there is a slight improvement in projected short-term spending over the next 12 months for durable goods, the study said.
Short-term spending prospects remained stable for housing, but reduced for car purchases, Isco said.
